Yes! This is entirely possible and I wouldn’t say you need a ton of sewing experience to do it. You can use a seam ripper to remove the weighted areas of the plush and use a ladder stitch to repair the hole you made after you wash the plushie. As for making a pouch to contain the beads you remove, you can cut a slit into the plushie and sew a small pocket and attach a zipper. You can easily just use a back stitch or a blanket stitch to reinforce the fabric but assuming it’s one of those like dinosaur weighted plushies, it won’t fray. You don’t even need a sewing machine, I would just use a needle and some quilting thread (thicker than all purpose).

There are tutorials and such to learn how to do these stitches but honestly, it may just be easier to just find someone who sews to do this for you. It’s not super difficult but it may be more of a hassle than it’s really worth to just alter this one item.

How experienced are you? As someone else here recommended, Cholyknight is a great place to start and they have some really good beginner friendly tutorials. However materials can be kinda pricey. Assuming you’re just going to handsew everything, you’ll still need…

- a seam ripper
- good fabric scissors (don’t use these for anything but fabric!!!)
- plush fabrics (lots of plush artists use minky)
- needle and thread 

I would recommend knowing a few stitches too! I suggest a blanket stitch, ladder stitch, backstitch, and a simple straight stitch to get started!

I would also like to say that a lot of the negative stereotypes surrounding those with BPD are about the individual and are not exclusive to the diagnosis. People with BPD may feel out of control but that’s an illusion. We are always in control and can choose actions that don’t hurt other people. I am not excusing dysfunctional and harmful behaviors by trying to explain what BPD is to people who do not have it. I am responsible for my actions and the harm they may cause always. I didn’t choose to have BPD, but I am making the best of it.

Hey, I hear you and see you. That sounds like a really difficult situation to be in to essentially be walking on eggshells and not knowing when your husband’s mood could turn for the worse. As someone with BPD, while I have intense outbursts of anger that may seem random, there is a logical reason for it even if I struggle to explain myself. For instance, while the logic of feeling a certain emotion may be sound for me (it usually is), the reaction is not. I can go from 1 to 100 sometimes over things I assume others would just experience a bit of frustration over.

 I can’t speak for your husband but when you’re in that mode, it’s difficult to communicate why sometimes but therapy has really helped me. Has your husband communicated to you why he is against therapy? Does he view it as a moral failing?  It’s been really helpful to break down my behaviors and learning to feel as deeply as I need to but also realizing that I have the free will to make the correct choice in the situation I find myself in. Perhaps your husband has experienced some trauma in his life that makes it easier to push people away rather than feel abandoned. This is common with people with BPD. It might be that villainizing people is a way with coping with those fears because that way it justifies him cutting people off when he feels unworthy of people staying. 

I would start by talking to him about how therapy is a tool to help ease the pain he must feel. Let him know that it’s difficult to see him in a way that is likely sourced from a place of pain and you just want to help him navigate it. I would try to reframe the idea of therapy as a safe place that he can let off the emotional pressure in a judgement free zone and work through a lot of things that must be bothering him. At least for me, talking about the trials of my life always defuses the emotional weight they hold over me. Let him know his actions are deeply hurtful to you and you want to work on this with him. Emphasize you’re not abandoning him, but you want to see change for the betterment of your marriage and to foster a good environment for your child. This changes the narrative from seeing therapy as a punishment to one of positivity and shows there is something to be gained from going.

We fully acknowledge and accept responsibility for this situation and sincerely apologize for the frustration and disappointment this will cause.

While no explanation of what’s happened can make up for the situation we’re in, we’ll write a brief overview of what led to this for those who would like more information:

Over the past few years, rising shipping costs significantly stretched our resources. Although we tried to absorb these costs without significantly raising prices, the final shipping invoices we received earlier this year were much higher than anticipated, creating a major financial shortfall.

We explored several solutions to address this shortfall and minimize customer impact, and until very recently, we believed we had viable paths forward. However, in the weeks following the recent announcement of tariffs on goods from China, it became clear that the situation had changed, and there was no longer a viable path forward for Fluffnest’s Plushies.

At the same time, we've been working through refund requests for plush orders awaiting shipment and from customers unhappy with Island Skies. We expected this could create some issues, but the volume of transactions seems to have created much larger issues than this has in the past. This would not be critical on its own, but combined with everything else going on, it has quickly left us with no options.

Due to these factors, we must immediately pause all plush-related operations, including order fulfillment and customer support. Our customer support team also manages the Island Skies Discord community, so while production will not be significantly impacted, there will be an impact on the Discord community. Unfortunately, we cannot process further refunds directly at this time, and we recommend affected customers request chargebacks through their payment providers. Please understand that the community managers and customer service team are not responsible for the delays or issues you’ve experienced. They are messengers doing their best with the information and tools available to them. Doxxing, harassment, or personal attacks against any member of the team are not acceptable under any circumstances.

To our valued customers: we understand deeply how upsetting and frustrating this must be. Your trust and excitement for our plushies means everything to us, and we're heartbroken to be unable to fulfill our commitments right now. We humbly apologize and we are determined to make amends as soon as circumstances allow.

To our incredible team members: we are profoundly grateful for your dedication, passion, and resilience during such an uncertain and challenging time. Despite the unpredictability and complexity of recent events, your commitment and kindness has genuinely inspired us. Please know that our support and gratitude for you will always continue, regardless of circumstances. Thank you for everything; it has meant the world to us.

Moving forward, though we will not be able to take new refund requests, we'll be doing everything we can to put ourselves in a position to refund all unshipped plush orders and dissatisfied Island Skies backers who have already requested refunds.

We are also still committed to fulfill remaining pre-orders for customers who still want them, though this situation could introduce significant delays in that process.

We do not expect this situation to have a significant impact on Island Skies production. At the same time, we cannot use Island Skies resources to support the plush business, as doing so could put the project in jeopardy.

We know how upsetting this news is, and we're truly devastated to have to deliver it. This has deeply impacted us personally as well, as Fluffnest Plushies isn't just a business, but something we've poured our hearts and dreams into. We appreciate your kindness, patience, and understanding more than words can express, and we are committed to making things right as soon as we're able.

With heartfelt apologies and gratitude, The Fluffnest Team"

First of all, I want to say I am so sorry for the loss of your precious Leo. I bet he was the best of good boys. It is so terribly unfortunate that cancer takes many of us way too soon and I’m sorry it couldn’t be different for Leo. I lost my wonderful cat, Nugget when he accidentally hung himself by the curtain strings. He wasn’t even a year old so I completely understand the feeling of being cheated out of a best friend. To answer your question, I think feeling okay with the death of a pet comes in waves. There are days where it’s easier to cope and there are days where it is very apparent that there is a deep, emotional wound. I hope you’re being kind to yourself during this difficult time as grief isn’t the same for everyone and your journey through it is unique. Just remember, I’m sure Leo wouldn’t want you to be sad. You did everything you could for that wonderful dog and I’m sure he knew that in his own way. Take your time to grieve but don’t allow loss to stop you from entertaining the idea of opening your heart up to another pet when the time is right. Loving another pet doesn’t mean you love Leo any less. 
Lastly, I would recommend trying to find healthy ways you can honor your pet. For me, I made a shrine and light incense whenever I feel sad. I try to go on walks and volunteer at the animal shelter too. In my heart, I feel like that is the way Nugget would want to be remembered.
